raw:
<explanation>
Instructional prompt pattern: user is asking for a corrected version of a structured data entry, implying a template or format example follows.

The phrase "entry" signals a structured document format (e.g., XML, dictionary, or glossary), with "entry" repeated to show the pattern of multiple entries in a list.

Final token `<entry` opens an XML/HTML-style tag, requiring an immediate closing `>` or attribute, followed by structured content mirroring the "bad example" above.
"Here is a bad example of an entry.
<entry" — the repetition of `<entry` begins the corrected or new example, strongly constraining next tokens to be a tag attribute or closing `>` followed by dictionary/glossary-style content like `<head>`, `<body>`, or similar structured fields.
A dictionary entry format.</explanation>
